title: Friday Sermon 60 by Rashad Khalifa: Abrogation, Scripture Communities, and Quran 2:111–123 (1982-11-19)
date_note: Explicit in the filename. This is a separate same-day recording from Dean Mahmoud's sermon.
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/60 - Friday Sermon 19 Nov 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: A separate November 19, 1982 recording that begins mid-linguistic discussion and moves into an extended argument against intra-Quranic abrogation. Quran 5:48 is used to say different scripture communities received distinct laws and methods while the Quran confirms and supersedes earlier scripture. Questions concern Christian and Jewish practice, dietary law, pilgrimage, wine, and Jesus. Quran 2:111–123 then addresses exclusive salvation claims, proof, submission to God regardless of label, Jewish-Christian disputes, mosques, divine omnipresence, sonship, creation by command, demands for miracles, and lack of intercession. The closing discussion rejects the divinity of Jesus, examines Sura 19's sonship language, and raises textual and chronological objections involving Ishmael, Isaac, and the claimed three days of Jesus' burial.

sections.title: Quran 2:111–123, exclusive salvation, proof, submission, scripture disputes, mosques, and no intercession
sections.summary: Exclusive Jewish and Christian claims to Heaven are called wishful thinking and are challenged to provide proof. Quran 2:112 states that anyone who submits to God while living righteously has nothing to fear. The passage continues through Jewish-Christian mutual denial, deserted mosques, God's east and west, sonship, creation by command, demands for direct speech or miracles, resistance to the messenger, and the inability of anyone to ransom or intercede on Judgment Day.

sections.summary: The closing discussion says Jesus' perfection or sinlessness does not affect the God-alone principle and insists that Jesus is dead. Rashad argues that Genesis contradicts itself by naming Isaac as Abraham's only son after Ishmael had already been born, and says the traditional three-day burial of Jesus amounts to less than the stated duration when counted chronologically.
